description: Mechanics, waves and optics, oscillations, collisions, conservation, and fields.
instructions: All main questions carry the same number of marks.
Show enough working to make the model, assumptions, and sign conventions clear.
Begin each main question on a new page when working on paper.
label: Paper 1

questions.stem: A rescue sled of total mass \(180\,\mathrm{kg}\) crosses a mountain valley on a smooth curved track. It is released from rest at a station \(14.0\,\mathrm{m}\) above the lowest point of the track. At the lowest point the track is locally circular with radius \(22.0\,\mathrm{m}\). Treat the sled as a particle and neglect rolling resistance.
questions.title: Rescue sled on a curved valley track

parts.answer:
The sled starts from rest and mechanical energy is conserved. Taking the lowest point as zero gravitational potential energy,
\[
mgh= rac12mv^2.
\]
The mass cancels, so
\[
v=\sqrt{2gh}.
\]
With \(h=14.0\,\mathrm{m}\),
\[
v=\sqrt{2(9.81)(14.0)}
=16.6\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}.
\]
parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Use energy conservation to find the sled's speed at the lowest point.

parts.answer:
At the lowest point the acceleration toward the centre of curvature is centripetal:
\[
a_c= rac{v^2}{R}.
\]
Using \(v^2=2gh=274.68\,\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-2}}\),
\[
a_c= rac{274.68}{22.0}
=12.5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}.
\]
The direction is upward, toward the centre of the local circular arc.
parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude and direction of the sled's centripetal acceleration at the lowest point.

parts.answer:
At the lowest point the radial direction is upward. The forces in this direction are the normal force upward and weight downward, so
\[
N-mg=m rac{v^2}{R}.
\]
Therefore
\[
N=m\left(g+ rac{v^2}{R}ight).
\]
Numerically,
\[
N=180(9.81+12.5)
=4.01	imes10^3\,\mathrm{N}.
\]
parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find the normal force exerted by the track on the sled at the lowest point.

parts.answer:
The largest allowed normal force gives the largest allowed speed at the bottom:
\[
N_{\max}=m\left(g+ rac{v_{\max}^2}{R}ight).
\]
Thus
\[
v_{\max}=\sqrt{R\left( rac{N_{\max}}{m}-gight)}.
\]
With \(N_{\max}=4.50	imes10^3\,\mathrm{N}\),
\[
v_{\max}=\sqrt{22.0\left( rac{4500}{180}-9.81ight)}
=18.3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}.
\]
The corresponding release height follows from \(mgh_{\max}= rac12mv_{\max}^2\):
\[
h_{\max}= rac{v_{\max}^2}{2g}
= rac{(18.3)^2}{2(9.81)}
=17.0\,\mathrm{m}.
\]
The planned \(14.0\,\mathrm{m}\) release height is therefore within the limit.
parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: The track is rated for a maximum normal force of \(4.50\times10^3\,\mathrm{N}\) on this loaded sled at the lowest point. Find the maximum safe speed there and the corresponding maximum release height above the lowest point.

questions.stem: A motor drives a winch drum of radius \(0.120\,\mathrm{m}\) and moment of inertia \(0.360\,\mathrm{kg\,m^2}\). A light cord wrapped around the drum lifts a \(25.0\,\mathrm{kg}\) crate vertically without slipping. From rest, the motor torque is \(\tau(t)=36.0+4.00t\,\mathrm{N\,m}\), where \(t\) is in seconds. Friction in the bearings is negligible.
questions.title: Winch drum with changing torque

parts.answer:
Let upward motion of the crate and unwinding rotation of the drum be positive. For the crate,
\[
T-mg=ma=mR\alpha.
\]
For the drum,
\[
	au-TR=I\alpha.
\]
Eliminate \(T\) using \(T=m(g+R\alpha)\):
\[
	au-mgR-mR^2\alpha=I\alpha.
\]
Therefore
\[
\alpha(t)= rac{	au(t)-mgR}{I+mR^2}.
\]
Here \(mgR=(25.0)(9.81)(0.120)=29.4\,\mathrm{N\,m}\) and \(I+mR^2=0.360+25.0(0.120)^2=0.720\,\mathrm{kg\,m^2}\), so
\[
\alpha(t)= rac{6.57+4.00t}{0.720}
=9.13+5.56t\,\mathrm{rad\,s^{-2}}.
\]
parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the angular acceleration of the drum as a function of time.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the speed of the cord and crate after \(3.00\,\mathrm{s}\).

parts.answer:
The angular displacement is
\[
	heta(t)=\int_0^t\omega(t')\,dt'
= rac{9.13t^2}{2}+ rac{2.78t^3}{3}.
\]
At \(3.00\,\mathrm{s}\),
\[
	heta=66.1\,\mathrm{rad},\qquad h=R	heta=(0.120)(66.1)=7.93\,\mathrm{m}.
\]
The work done by the motor becomes rotational kinetic energy, translational kinetic energy, and gravitational potential energy:
\[
W= rac12I\omega^2+ rac12mv^2+mgh.
\]
Thus
\[
W= rac12(0.360)(52.4)^2+ rac12(25.0)(6.29)^2+(25.0)(9.81)(7.93)
=2.93	imes10^3\,\mathrm{J}.
\]
parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find the work done by the motor during the first \(3.00\,\mathrm{s}\).

parts.answer:
Instantaneous motor power is torque times angular speed:
\[
P=	au\omega.
\]
At \(t=3.00\,\mathrm{s}\),
\[
	au=36.0+4.00(3.00)=48.0\,\mathrm{N\,m}.
\]
Therefore
\[
P=(48.0)(52.4)
=2.51	imes10^3\,\mathrm{W}.
\]
parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Calculate the instantaneous power delivered by the motor at \(t=3.00\,\mathrm{s}\).

parts.answer: The motor torque must exceed \(mgR\) to give a positive upward angular acceleration from rest. If \(\tau<mgR\), the crate would not start lifting upward; if it were already moving upward, it would slow down.
parts.label: (e)
parts.prompt: State what would happen if the applied torque were less than \(mgR\).

questions.stem:
A compact camera is calibrated by photographing a flat test chart \(2.40\,\mathrm{m}\) in front of a thin converging lens of focal length \(12.0\,\mathrm{mm}\). The entrance pupil is a circular aperture of diameter \(3.00\,\mathrm{mm}\), and the calibration light has wavelength \(550\,\mathrm{nm}\).

For a circular aperture, the Airy/Rayleigh angular radius is
\[
\theta_R=1.22\frac{\lambda}{D},
\]
where \(D\) is the aperture diameter.
questions.title: Camera calibration and diffraction limit

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the image distance from the lens to the sensor plane.

parts.answer:
The lateral magnification is
\[
m=- rac{s'}{s}.
\]
Thus
\[
m=- rac{0.01206}{2.40}
=-5.03	imes10^{-3}.
\]
For a \(1.20\,\mathrm{m}\) high chart, the image height is
\[
h'=mh=(-5.03	imes10^{-3})(1.20)
=-6.03	imes10^{-3}\,\mathrm{m}.
\]
The image is inverted and has height \(6.03\,\mathrm{mm}\).
parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the magnification and the image height of a \(1.20\,\mathrm{m}\) high calibration chart.

parts.answer:
For a circular aperture, the angular radius of the Airy disk to the first minimum is approximately
\[
	heta=1.22 rac{\lambda}{D}.
\]
With \(\lambda=550	imes10^{-9}\,\mathrm{m}\) and \(D=3.00	imes10^{-3}\,\mathrm{m}\),
\[
	heta=1.22 rac{550	imes10^{-9}}{3.00	imes10^{-3}}
=2.24	imes10^{-4}\,\mathrm{rad}.
\]
The radius of the central bright spot on the sensor is approximately
\[
r=s'	heta=(0.01206)(2.24	imes10^{-4})
=2.70	imes10^{-6}\,\mathrm{m}.
\]
So the Airy radius on the sensor is \(2.70\,\mu\mathrm{m}\).
parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Estimate the diffraction-limited angular radius of the Airy disk and its radius on the sensor.

parts.answer:
The Rayleigh criterion requires the angular separation to be at least about
\[
	heta_R=1.22 rac{\lambda}{D}=2.24	imes10^{-4}\,\mathrm{rad}.
\]
At an object distance of \(2.40\,\mathrm{m}\), the corresponding separation on the chart is
\[
x_{\min}=s	heta_R=(2.40)(2.24	imes10^{-4})
=5.37	imes10^{-4}\,\mathrm{m}
=0.537\,\mathrm{mm}.
\]
Two marks separated by \(0.800\,\mathrm{mm}\) have a larger angular separation than this, so they should be resolvable by the aperture alone.
parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Using the Rayleigh criterion, decide whether two fine marks \(0.800\,\mathrm{mm}\) apart on the chart can be resolved by the aperture.

parts.answer: Since \(\theta_R=1.22\lambda/D\), reducing the aperture diameter increases the diffraction angle. If the diameter is halved to \(1.50\,\mathrm{mm}\), the diffraction-limited angular radius doubles and the smallest resolvable separation on the chart also doubles.
parts.label: (e)
parts.prompt: State how the diffraction-limited resolution changes if the aperture diameter is reduced to \(1.50\,\mathrm{mm}\).

questions.section: Section C: Oscillations and Collisions, Conservation and Fields
questions.stem: A small floating service platform has vertical sides, horizontal waterline area \(3.20\,\mathrm{m^2}\), and mass \(240\,\mathrm{kg}\). It floats in fresh water of density \(1000\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}\). For small vertical displacements, neglect damping and assume the waterline area remains constant.
questions.title: Floating platform oscillations

parts.answer:
At equilibrium the buoyant force equals the weight:
\[
ho gAx_0=Mg.
\]
Therefore the equilibrium draft is
\[
x_0= rac{M}{ho A}
= rac{240}{(1000)(3.20)}
=7.50	imes10^{-2}\,\mathrm{m}.
\]
So the platform sinks \(0.0750\,\mathrm{m}\) below the water surface at equilibrium.
parts.label: (a)

parts.answer:
If the platform is displaced downward by \(y\) from equilibrium, the extra displaced volume is \(Ay\). The extra buoyant force is upward and has magnitude
\[
ho gAy.
\]
Thus the restoring force is
\[
F=-ho gAy,
\]
which has the SHM form \(F=-ky\) with
\[
k_{\mathrm{eff}}=ho gA=(1000)(9.81)(3.20)=3.14	imes10^4\,\mathrm{N\,m^{-1}}.
\]
parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Show that a small vertical displacement gives simple harmonic motion and find the effective spring constant.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Calculate the platform's angular frequency and frequency of vertical oscillation.

parts.answer:
With the payload, the total mass is
\[
M'=240+160=400\,\mathrm{kg}.
\]
The new equilibrium draft is
\[
x_0'= rac{400}{(1000)(3.20)}
=0.125\,\mathrm{m}.
\]
The effective spring constant is unchanged because the waterline area is unchanged. The new frequency is
\[
f'= rac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{ rac{3.1392	imes10^4}{400}}
=1.41\,\mathrm{Hz}.
\]
The added payload increases the inertia, so the oscillation frequency decreases.
parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: A \(160\,\mathrm{kg}\) payload is placed on the platform. Find the new equilibrium draft and the new oscillation frequency.

parts.answer:
For the loaded platform, \(M'=400\,\mathrm{kg}\) and \(k_{\mathrm{eff}}=3.1392	imes10^4\,\mathrm{N\,m^{-1}}\). If it is released from rest at amplitude \(A_0=0.0400\,\mathrm{m}\), the mechanical energy is
\[
E= rac12k_{\mathrm{eff}}A_0^2
= rac12(3.1392	imes10^4)(0.0400)^2
=25.1\,\mathrm{J}.
\]
The maximum speed occurs at equilibrium:
\[
v_{\max}=\omega' A_0=\sqrt{ rac{k_{\mathrm{eff}}}{M'}}A_0.
\]
Thus
\[
v_{\max}=\sqrt{ rac{3.1392	imes10^4}{400}}(0.0400)
=0.354\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}.
\]
parts.label: (e)
parts.prompt: With the payload on board, the platform is pushed \(0.0400\,\mathrm{m}\) below its new equilibrium position and released from rest. Find the oscillation energy and maximum speed.
